# Per-file SERVER test durations, one per line as  <duration_ms><TAB><path>, longest first
# (duration descending, path ascending on ties). scripts/test.sh reads this to dispatch the server
# phase LONGEST-FIRST (see its "longest-first server dispatch" block). It is a DATA file, not a
# script: a new scripts/*.mjs would be picked up by scripts/tsconfig.json (allowJs+checkJs+strict)
# and red the whole suite via `npm run typecheck`.
# Lines starting with # and blank lines are skipped. Any other line that does not match
# ^[0-9]+<TAB>server/...test.(ts|js)$ makes test.sh FAIL OPEN to the collected alphabetical order
# (see the AC in tasks/gap-suite-server-dispatch-longest-first-and-parallel-static-stages.md and the
# "server dispatch" criteria in server/shared/tests/quay-test-script.test.ts). A row is a dispatch
# ORDER hint only: a collected file with no row is not skipped — it is dispatched after the listed
# ones, keeping its collected order.
# DATA SOURCE: round 1924 of the main checkout ledger
#   /data/home/yale/work/claudecodeui/.quay/verification-round.jsonl
# Green (fail=0, pass=885, durationMs=286799, plannedFiles=507, startedAt 2026-11-03T14:13:10Z) and
# it is the most recent green round at generation time (2026-11-04). It carries all 507 server test
# files the tree collected then: the same 507 `find server -name '*.test.ts' -o -name '*.test.js' |
# grep -v node_modules | sort` collects on this tree — 0 missing, 0 extra, 0 duplicates.
# REGENERATE (prints the data body on stdout; keep THIS header above it, then diff):

#   node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const rows=fs.readFileSync(process.argv[1],"utf8").trim().split("
").map(l=>{try{return JSON.parse(l)}catch{return null}}).filter(Boolean);const g=rows.find(r=>r.round===1924&&r.fail===0&&Array.isArray(r.perFile));const s=g.perFile.filter(p=>p.file.startsWith("server/")).sort((a,b)=>b.durationMs-a.durationMs||(a.file<b.file?-1:1));process.stdout.write(s.map(p=>p.durationMs+"	"+p.file).join("
")+"
")' /data/home/yale/work/claudecodeui/.quay/verification-round.jsonl
# The source round is PINNED (r.round===1924) rather than selected as "the latest green": the ledger
# gains a green round every few minutes, so a "latest" selector would print different bytes on every
# re-run and this file could never be re-verified against its own documented command. Re-pin the
# number — and update DATA SOURCE above — when the baseline is deliberately refreshed (that is what
# gap-quay-test-script-runner-self-overhead did to replace the stale round-636 body).
